statements.impact_statement: The shipped Extra CODEOWNERS service uses Python zlib.compress and decompressobj for bounded in-memory discovery-cache bodies, not the C gz* file-writer interface. CPython's zlib extensions on amd64 and arm64 import deflate/inflate and checksum APIs, with no gz* imports. A scan of all 778 ELF files in each published image found gz* imports only in dpkg-deb and libapt-pkg; application entrypoints, HTTP routes, healthchecks and migrations neither invoke those programs nor load the APT library. The vulnerable gzip-writer path is outside the reviewed service execution path. The Debian zlib1g package remains present and unpatched. This does not cover operator-run package management, custom FFI or plugins, arbitrary commands, or execution after compromise.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-109518 requires APT to acquire and install packages over attacker-controlled HTTP while following redirects and retrying downloads. The shipped Extra CODEOWNERS entrypoint, healthcheck, migrations and application routes run Python; they do not invoke APT, load its Python bindings or expose its package-acquisition API. GitHub requests use HTTPX, not APT. The vulnerable APT acquisition/install code is therefore outside the reviewed service execution path. The apt packages remain present and unpatched. This assessment does not cover operator-run package installation, custom code or plugins, or arbitrary execution after compromise.
statements.status_notes: Debian identifies apt 3.0.3 as vulnerable and trixie's 3.0.4 as fixed. This is a runtime reachability assessment, not a package fix or component-absence claim. Source: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-109518. Reviewed Python entrypoint/CLI, ASGI routes, GitHub HTTPX client, migration commands and Dockerfile; no APT invocation or adapter is used. The runtime binding records the reviewed code, dependency lock and Docker inputs. Raw scan findings and the empty scanner ignore list are retained.

statements.impact_statement: The service does not process CMS, S/MIME or PKCS#7 messages or call CMS APIs. Psycopg's bundled OpenSSL 3.5.4 is reached through libpq's TLS client and authentication paths, not the affected CMS message parser/decryptor. Source entrypoint review and static inspection of all 17 amd64/18 arm64 Psycopg native payloads found no CMS or CMP imports. Import absence supports the source review; it is not standalone proof of every internal library call. This assessment covers only the shipped Linux amd64 and arm64 Extra CODEOWNERS service, not operator-run commands, plugins, custom FFI, execution after compromise or other builds. The library is present and unpatched; this is not a blanket OpenSSL exclusion.

This assessment covers only the shipped Linux amd64 and arm64 Extra CODEOWNERS service, not operator-run commands, plugins, custom FFI, execution after compromise or other builds. The library is present and unpatched; this is not a blanket OpenSSL exclusion.
